title: FastPath: A Hybrid Approach for Efficient Hardware Security Verification
problem: Microarchitectural information leakage verification methods suffer individual weaknesses: formal methods lack scalability, simulation lacks exhaustiveness, and existing approaches have limited flexibility for changing security requirements.
motivation: Verification methods for detecting information leakage in hardware designs must be simultaneously scalable, exhaustive, and flexible to meet diverse and evolving security requirements.
method: FastPath combines simulation efficiency with formal verification exhaustiveness via a hybrid methodology that employs structural analysis to automate the verification process, enabling practical deployment in existing verification flows.
key_novelty: Hybrid simulation-plus-formal verification framework with structural automation for microarchitectural security verification.
contributions: Hybrid verification methodology combining simulation efficiency and formal exhaustiveness
Structural analysis framework to automate security verification
Significant reduction in manual effort while maintaining exhaustive confidence
Discovery and fix of previously unknown operand leak in cv32e40s RISC-V processor

metrics.other: Significant reduction in manual verification effort with same exhaustiveness level

limitations: Not discussed; evaluation focused on security verification workflow integration.
primary_theme: Hybrid formal-simulation security verification with structural automation
